metadata.laymanSummary: Rep. John Larson, the lead sponsor of Social Security 2100 through multiple Congresses, voted for his own bill and delivered an impassioned floor speech after it narrowly failed.

data.name: John Larson
data.position: Representative · CT-1 · House Ways and Means

data.quote: I have introduced this bill in seven consecutive Congresses. Every time, we have been told to wait. Wait for a better moment. Wait for a different majority. Wait for the stars to align. Meanwhile, the Trust Fund gets eight years closer to depletion. I am done waiting. Every member of this House who voted no today will have to answer to every senior in their district when their Social Security check is 23% smaller. I will be introducing this bill again in the next Congress. And the next. Until America keeps the promise it made to its workers.
data.speaker: John Larson
data.context: House floor statement after H.R.6001 failed 208-225

data.billName: Social Security 2100: A Sacred Trust Act

data.title: Rep. Larson's Social Security 2100 Campaign
data.text: Rep. Larson has been the primary champion of Social Security 2100 legislation since 2019. The bill has consistently attracted more than 180 Democratic co-sponsors in each Congress but has never received a Republican vote. The Social Security Trustees project the Trust Fund will be depleted by 2033, triggering automatic 23% benefit cuts for all recipients.
